title: The ext4 inode number starts from 1 and the position within the group starts from 0
summary: If there are N inodes in each group, the number ino belongs to group (ino−1)//N, and the index within the group is (ino−1)%N.
applies: ext4 file system image; Linux kernel format document
detail: The index multiplied by s_inode_size is the byte offset within the corresponding inode table; the inode table location is obtained from the group descriptor.
boundary: Inode table layout is affected by file system characteristics, and it cannot be directly assumed that each group places its own table at the same relative block number.
relevance: Avoid misalignment of the entire group when locating inodes just on group boundaries.
